title: 47 U.S.C. § 222 — Privacy of Customer Proprietary Network Information
short_name: CPNI — Carrier Duty to Protect Customer Information
court: FCC (regulatory enforcement); U.S. District Courts (§ 207 private right of action)
domain: telecommunications, CPNI, SIM swap authentication, carrier duty of care
last_material_amendment: FCC Second Report and Order, WC Docket No. 21-441 (2024 SIM Swap rules)
filed_by: Claude (assistant) under steward direction — Michael Hartmann
cases_to_add: FCC In re T-Mobile USA (2022) — $91.25M settlement for CPNI failures enabling SIM swap fraud
FCC In re Verizon (2024) — enforcement action for SIM swap authentication failures post-2024 rules
steward_relevance: The AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile SIM swaps enabling Christina Cerretani's call interception and account takeover were violations of § 222(c)(1) — carrier disclosed CPNI (phone number identity, account access) to unauthorized parties (the SIM swap requestor) without approval of the customer (steward). The 2024 FCC SIM swap rules (WC Docket 21-441) also apply to events after their effective date.
first_step_triage: Request CPNI access logs from each carrier under § 222(c)(2) (customer right to own CPNI on request). This gives evidence of: what was disclosed, to whom, when. File FCC complaint for each carrier (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile) under § 208 as prerequisite to § 207 private right of action. FCC complaint also creates official record for civil litigation.
